plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids or strategies. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks losses if I win at a higher price, while bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and given the theoretical guarantee that truthful bidding maximizes expected profit in second-price auctions, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding my true value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses when I shouldn't win. Bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no history to adjust against, truthful bidding is optimal.

Bidding exactly $20 ensures that if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (which will be less than my value, guaranteeing non-negative profit), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me, which is the correct outcome.
